text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Liamine Zeroual announces the creation of a special fund to finance development in the country's southern provinces. The fund, effective in 1998, will draw on part of oil and gas taxes.
- The Transitional National Council (CNT) debates draft law over new territorial status of Algiers, stretching the capital's current boundaries.

- The government-appointed CNT will be dissolved on May 18 but its members will keep their privileges, including a hefty retirement pension, official cars and diplomatic passports. The CNT will be replaced by an elected National Assembly after June 5 general elections.
- Security forces were encircling about 50 "terrorists" in Ain Defla region, southwest of Algiers.
- The Social and Economic National Council holds its 8th session to assess the government's programme but the session was lacklustre and dominated by ritual reading of half-year report.
- The authorities and political parties to hold a meeting to draw lots to allocate airtimes for the election candidates on the state-run radio and television.
